final.memo:
Bath & Body Works is a leading specialty retailer with a powerful brand, currently mispriced by a market overly focused on post-pandemic normalization [D01], [D05]. At current levels, the company trades at a 7.8x trailing P/E and 5.5x EV/EBITDA, valuations that fundamentally ignore the strength of its underlying cash-generative model [D04].

The business currently operates at a 15% margin, trailing peers like Ulta Beauty and Church & Dwight, who maintain margins between 17% and 19.7% [D06]. We believe there is a direct path to closing this gap through disciplined organizational simplification and focused merchandise-margin initiatives [D06]. By reaching a 19% operating margin, we see a clear path to a $65 share price over the next three years [D06].

The market has wrongly conflated short-term cyclical retail pressures with the long-term earnings power of the business [D05]. Our focus is on the leadership transition; the current interim CEO structure creates an opening to ensure the board appoints a permanent leader with the necessary retail operational expertise to unlock value [D01].

Our plan is to engage privately with Executive Chair Sarah Nash and the board to expedite the search for a permanent CEO and to formalize margin targets [D01]. We view this as a primary catalyst for the company to regain its operational excellence [D01]. Should the board fail to act with urgency, we are prepared to escalate our engagement [D02]. We are initiating a 5% position in the common stock, sized to our high-conviction assessment of the current risk-reward, while hedging systemic retail beta with index puts [D04], [D05].
